_readme: Concept bank for the Hamdam reel series. The agent READS this file and never writes to it. After a concept ships, set used=true by hand. When fewer than three entries have used=false, write more - do not let the agent improvise one.
_verification_status: DRAFT - arguments, insights and lessons drafted by Claude and must be read and approved by Ealia. Claims flagged in _check are the ones worth verifying.
_page_note: Reel pages: 0 scene, 1 headline, 2 Persian verse, 3 English translation with the poet line beneath, 4 insightFa/insightEn - the philological point, on screen rather than buried in the caption, 5 lessonFa/lessonEn then sendFa/sendEn. Page 4 is the page nobody else can copy; keep it to one sharp claim that is true. insightEn, lessonEn, sendEn and headline must be Latin script ONLY - Source Serif has no Arabic glyphs, so a Persian word inside an English line renders as tofu boxes. Transliterate instead (anqa, simurgh, ghazal).
_mood_key: Pairs the concept with a background from make_backgrounds.py and a track from the Drive 11Labs folder. happy = bright Mahur; love = romantic Mahur; grave = restrained, sparse; wry = light but not celebratory. Never put a love or happy bed under a grave concept.

concepts.headline: THE NEEDLE ANSWERS BACK
concepts.argument:
A shirt complains to a needle about the wounds it leaves. The needle replies: if you don't like my way, go and speak to the tailor.

This is the مناظره - the debate poem, and Parvin's signature form. Two ordinary objects argue and one of them wins. She gives speech to needles, to thorns, to crows, to the smallest and least regarded thing in the room, and the wisdom almost always belongs to the humbler party.

The needle's answer is also a refusal to be blamed for a design it did not choose. It points past itself, to the hand that guides it.
concepts.insightFa: پروین حکمت را به سوزن می‌دهد، نه به پیراهن
concepts.insightEn: Parvin gives the wisdom to the needle, not the shirt.
concepts.lessonFa: تو مقصرِ طرحی نیستی که به دستت داده‌اند
concepts.lessonEn: You are not to blame for a design you did not choose
concepts.sendFa: برای کسی بفرست که این روزها ناحق سرزنش شده
concepts.sendEn: Send this to someone who's been blamed unfairly
concepts.poetLineFa: پروین اعتصامی — تبریز و تهران، قرن بیستم
concepts.poetLineEn: Parvin Etesami — Tabriz and Tehran, 20th century
concepts._check: مناظره as Parvin's signature form is well established. Published 12 Aug 2026: instagram.com/reel/Db6pltQmBrE/

concepts.headline: THAT HANDLE WAS SOMEONE'S ARM
concepts.argument:
Khayyam looks at a clay jug and says: this was a lover once. The handle you are holding was an arm around someone's neck.

In English, Khayyam usually arrives softened - wistful, Victorian, a little melancholy. The Persian is not wistful. It is a physicist's observation delivered flat: matter is conserved, the dead become the cup, and you are drinking from someone.

That is what makes it frightening rather than pretty. He is not being poetic about death. He is being accurate.
concepts.insightFa: در ترجمه، خیام حسرت‌زده می‌شود؛ در فارسی فقط دقیق است
concepts.insightEn: In translation Khayyam sounds wistful. In Persian he is simply being accurate.
concepts.lessonFa: هر چیزِ ساده‌ای که در دست داری، روزی کسی بوده
concepts.lessonEn: Everything ordinary in your hands was once someone
concepts.sendFa: برای کسی بفرست که قدرِ لحظه را می‌داند
concepts.sendEn: Send this to someone who knows what a moment is worth
concepts._check: Khayyam of Nishapur, 11th-12th century - safe. That English translations soften him is a widely held critical view, phrased as comparison rather than a claim about any named translator.

concepts.headline: SHE PUT SOCRATES IN A PERSIAN QASIDA
concepts.argument:
Someone asks Socrates what he has learned of death. He answers with a question: why do you call this life?

A 20th-century Iranian woman writing in classical Persian form, arguing with a Greek philosopher who died 2,300 years earlier. Persian poetry has always done this - absorbed what it met and answered back in its own metre.

Parvin is usually taught, when she is taught at all, as the gentle one who wrote about flowers and mothers. She was also this.
concepts.insightFa: زنی ایرانی در قرن بیستم، در وزن کلاسیک فارسی، با سقراط بحث می‌کند
concepts.insightEn: A 20th-century Iranian woman arguing with Socrates, in classical Persian metre.
concepts.lessonFa: پرسیدن، خودش نیمی از زندگی است
concepts.lessonEn: To keep asking is already half of living
concepts.sendFa: برای کسی بفرست که هیچ‌وقت از پرسیدن دست نکشید
concepts.sendEn: Send this to someone who never stopped asking
concepts.poetLineFa: پروین اعتصامی — تبریز و تهران، قرن بیستم
concepts.poetLineEn: Parvin Etesami — Tabriz and Tehran, 20th century
concepts._check: The poem itself names Socrates. Parvin lived 1907-1941. 'Usually taught as the gentle one' is a characterisation of reception - soften or cut if you disagree.

concepts.headline: BEFORE THE GRASS GROWS FROM YOU
concepts.argument:
Sit on the grass and live well for a few days - before the grass grows out of you.

The English phrase for this is carpe diem, and it flattens the poem. Horace says seize the day because time flies. Khayyam says something colder: you are the soil. The grass you are sitting on and the grass that will grow from you are the same grass.

The consolation and the threat are the same sentence.
concepts.insightFa: این «دم را دریاب» نیست — خیام می‌گوید تو خودِ خاکی
concepts.insightEn: This is not carpe diem. Khayyam is saying you are the soil.
concepts.lessonFa: امروز را از دست نده؛ همین است که داری
concepts.lessonEn: Do not lose today - it is the part you actually hold
concepts.sendFa: برای کسی بفرست که این روزها فرصت نشستن ندارد
concepts.sendEn: Send this to someone who hasn't had a moment to sit
concepts._check: The Horace comparison is interpretation - cut it if it feels like showing off.

concepts.headline: A SPARROW TELLS A PIGEON TO LEAVE
concepts.argument:
At dawn a sparrow tells a pigeon: put your head out of the nest. The horizons are bright - why are you sleeping in the dark?

Note which bird is speaking. The گنجشک is the smallest and most ordinary bird in Persian verse, the one nobody writes about. The کبوتر is the poet's bird, the noble one. Parvin hands the wisdom to the sparrow and the excuses to the pigeon.

She does this everywhere. The lesser party is right.
concepts.insightFa: گنجشک عادی‌ترین پرندهٔ شعر فارسی است، و پروین حرفِ درست را به او می‌دهد
concepts.insightEn: The sparrow is the most ordinary bird in Persian verse. Parvin gives it the right answer.
concepts.lessonFa: گاهی کوچک‌ترین صدا، درست‌ترین حرف را می‌زند
concepts.lessonEn: Sometimes the smallest voice is the one that is right
concepts.sendFa: برای کسی بفرست که وقتِ بیرون آمدنش رسیده
concepts.sendEn: Send this to someone whose time to step out has come
concepts.poetLineFa: پروین اعتصامی — تبریز و تهران، قرن بیستم
concepts.poetLineEn: Parvin Etesami — Tabriz and Tehran, 20th century
concepts._check: The relative poetic status of گنجشک vs کبوتر is a judgement about convention - defensible but worth a native reader's eye.

concepts.headline: THE PHOENIX IS NO ONE'S PREY
concepts.argument:
The phoenix is nobody's prey. Take your trap back - all it ever catches is wind.

The bird is the عنقا, and the joke is that it does not exist. You cannot trap it because there is nothing there to trap. Hafez is not saying you have failed to catch it. He is saying the hunt was the mistake.

He wrote a great deal of this kind of line, and it is the part of him English quote accounts almost never carry - Hafez the sceptic, unimpressed, slightly amused at your equipment.
concepts.insightFa: عنقا وجود ندارد — برای همین به دام نمی‌افتد
concepts.insightEn: The anqa is a bird that does not exist. That is why no trap can hold it.
concepts.lessonFa: بعضی چیزها را نمی‌شود گرفت؛ می‌شود دوست داشت
concepts.lessonEn: Some things cannot be caught - only loved
concepts.sendFa: برای کسی بفرست که سخت دنبالِ چیزی است
concepts.sendEn: Send this to someone chasing something hard
concepts._check: عنقا confirmed present in the Persian of hafez-004. insightEn transliterates it as 'anqa' because Source Serif cannot render Arabic script.

concepts.headline: THE PART IS PULLED TOWARD ITS WHOLE
concepts.argument:
This is homesickness - and not the metaphorical kind. Rumi's family fled Balkh ahead of the Mongols when he was a boy. He never went back. He died in Konya, about 3,000 km from where he was born.

He wrote about longing for home because he was someone who couldn't go home.
concepts.insightFa: مولانا کودک بود که از بلخ گریخت، و هرگز بازنگشت
concepts.insightEn: Rumi fled Balkh as a boy and never went back.
concepts.lessonFa: دلتنگی نشانه‌ی ضعف نیست؛ نشانه‌ی ریشه است
concepts.lessonEn: Homesickness is not weakness - it is proof of roots
concepts.sendFa: برای کسی بفرست که دور از خانه است
concepts.sendEn: Send this to someone far from home
concepts.poetLineFa: مولانا — بلخ و قونیه، قرن سیزدهم
concepts._check: Published by hand 7 August 2026. Kept as the format reference.
